hypothesis: A different decomposition solver -- the Riemann-Roch (Nagao) family developed in solver_05/07/08 -- changes what is findable on the real ECC2K-130 curve, not only on the toy ladder. Run it against the matched Semaev controls on E: y^2+xy=x^3+1 over GF(2^131) with identical factor base, arity, targets, modes and all-phase budgets.
curve: K_0 : y^2 + xy = x^3 + 1 over GF(2^131) in the repository's permuted type-II ONB model (curves.Curve over nagaoannihilator.CountedField(131)). This is the ECC2K-130 challenge curve; its group order is checked against the Koblitz recurrence at startup.
factor_base: F = { P in E(GF(2^131)) : x(P) in V \ {0} }, V = span of the first d ONB basis vectors. Identical for every variant. m = 3 summands, x_i distinct, x_i != 0, x_i != x(R), exactly as in solver_04..09.
targets: Four per stratum per panel, minted fresh under seed 20260916 and never used in solver_02..09. Stratum 'uniform': R = pointFromX(x) for uniform random x in GF(2^131), i.e. a uniform affine point of the full curve group. Stratum 'known_decomposable': R = P1+P2+P3 for a random triple of distinct factor-base points, so a relation provably exists and the planted triple is recorded. The planted stratum is a constructed existence witness, NOT a natural-yield estimate: at d in {6,7} and n = 131, m*d is 18 or 21 against 131, so a uniform target has expected decomposition count about 2^-100 and is expected to have none.
method: Every variant is run unmodified from its own frozen folder: quadratic-optimized = solver_07/optimized.cell, quadratic-image = solver_08/image_solver.cell, s4-symmetric and chained-s3 = the solver_06 runCell frontends. Only the driver is new. No variant sees the planted triple.
validation: (1) Group order from the Koblitz recurrence equals 4*r with r the published 129-bit ECC2K-130 prime. (2) Every factor-base point and every target is re-checked on the curve. (3) Every reported relation is re-verified independently of the solver that produced it: each abscissa is lifted with pointFromX, membership in V and the exclusions are re-checked, and the signed group sum is recomputed and compared with the target. (4) On the planted stratum, any run reporting status 'complete' must contain the planted triple; a complete run that misses it is a correctness failure. (5) No exhaustive oracle exists at n = 131, so a 'complete' set is complete with respect to this factor base and arity by exhaustion of the solver's candidate space, not by an independent enumeration of the group.
primary_metric: All-phase seconds and counted field API operations per resolved instance, matched across variants on identical targets; and, for the planted stratum, seconds to the first independently verified relation.
falsification: The RR family is shown to carry no advantage at full size if it resolves no more target/mode slots than the Semaev controls under the same budget. It is shown to be incorrect at full size if any reported relation fails the independent lift-and-sum check, or if a complete planted run misses its planted triple. A timeout is not negative mathematical evidence: it establishes only that this implementation, budget and panel did not resolve that slot.
limits: This measures an ORACLE at full field size with a factor base far below the existence threshold m*d >= 131 + log2(m!) (d = 45 at m = 3). It therefore establishes nothing about the end-to-end attack: no full-DLP S, no rho ratio, and no relation yield are claimed or computed from these runs. Uniform-stratum enumerations are expected to be empty and are measured for cost, not for yield. Python field arithmetic in the ONB model is uncalibrated against the repository's GPU/Rust cost model; SAT work has no matching unit against counted field operations, so the SAT rows are compared on resolved slots and wall clock only. Targets are points of the full group E(GF(2^131)), not restricted to the order-r subgroup; decomposition is a group-law question and the restriction is irrelevant to it, but no claim about <G> is made. Single sequential run, no repeated-trial statistics.
